excerpt: Compare ready and off-plan property in Sharjah using ownership eligibility, inspection, payment timing, handover and the full cost.
introduction:
A ready Sharjah property can be inspected before purchase; an off-plan property is bought under a contract before completion. The choice depends on when you need the home, the buyer's ownership right, the complete payment schedule and your ability to manage delivery or financing changes.

Compare actual properties on the same basis. The worked payment example below shows how instalments can be organised across the purchase.
takeaways: Inspect a ready home and verify title, seller authority, building charges and any existing tenancy.
For off-plan, check project registration, contract, payment recipient, instalments and handover terms.
Confirm foreign ownership eligibility for the exact unit and keep a reserve for unexpected costs.

sections.heading: What can you verify before buying?
sections.body:
For a ready apartment or villa, visit the actual property, inspect its condition and shared areas, and check parking, utilities and access. Review the title, seller's authority, any mortgage or tenancy, outstanding charges and required clearance. Confirm the occupation status and the agreed date for possession.

For off-plan, request the registered project and unit details, signed plan and specification, construction progress, instalment schedule and handover provisions. A show home or rendering may not match the apartment or villa in the contract. Ask the authority and developer how the buyer's interest is registered.

The [Aljada and Al Mamsha comparison](/journal/aljada-vs-al-mamsha-apartment-buying-comparison) shows how the particular phase and building matter to a Sharjah apartment decision.

sections.heading: Compare payment timing and total cost
sections.body:
Imagine an off-plan price of AED 1,000,000 payable as 20% at booking, 40% during construction and 40% at handover. The amounts are AED 200,000, AED 400,000 and AED 400,000. This is a sample schedule, not a Sharjah offer. Registration, finance, furnishing and other charges are additional.

The chart shows the components of that single price. Put the actual dates and conditions on a calendar and include current rent until the home is ready. Review the full purchase price and the dates of all remaining instalments.

For a ready property, ask when the deposit, balance, loan and transfer charges are due. Compare the two options with your available cash and a separate contingency, not only their first payments.

sections.heading: Confirm ownership and official costs
sections.body:
Ask Sharjah's registration department to confirm the right available to your nationality for the exact property. The [Sharjah ownership eligibility guide](/journal/how-to-check-foreign-ownership-eligibility-in-sharjah) explains why an approved project count or developer brochure does not establish every buyer's right.

The Sharjah Executive Council's [property sale service listing](https://ec.shj.ae/en/government-service-details?serviceId=7804877f29e1d98d856134f4180a0517ef859c39c3ca891bc3a13e3773b7316bf5fcd08d2966872ceec3e0acf29842ff) describes a title transfer service. Confirm the current process and itemised charges for the specific ready or off-plan transaction. Do not assume the same fee or document applies in every case.

Check the seller or developer's authority, any mortgage, lease and required clearance. Verify payment instructions independently and keep receipts and the registered outcome.

sections.heading: Consider handover and ongoing expenses
sections.body:
A ready property may need immediate repairs, while an off-plan buyer must allow for the possibility that completion or a planned facility changes. Read the agreement's provisions on delay, specifications, default and cancellation. Ask a qualified adviser to explain any unclear term.

Request the current or estimated service charges, their calculation basis and the services covered. Include insurance, utilities, maintenance and, for a villa, any garden or equipment upkeep. An estimate for an unfinished project is not necessarily a fixed future charge.

If you intend to let the unit, allow time for handover, repairs and tenant search. A scheduled completion date is not a guarantee of rental income.

sections.heading: Test finance and the downside
sections.body:
Ask the lender for current eligibility, valuation, loan amount, fees, insurance and the repayment schedule for each property. A developer plan and a bank mortgage are different obligations. Test a lower valuation, delayed approval and a change in your income.

Keep funds available for the contractual payments and a repair reserve. Do not rely on an assumed future sale or rent to pay an instalment unless you can manage if it does not arrive.

Compare genuinely similar alternatives and the value of being able to inspect or use a home sooner. Neither completion status guarantees capital growth.

sections.heading: Compare the location and intended use
sections.body:
Test work and school routes from the actual property and ask whether the facilities you need are open today. If the home is an investment, seek recent signed leases and completed sales for comparable units, keeping asking prices separate. Deduct vacancy and owner costs from expected rent.

Write down any unresolved issue and the evidence needed to settle it before committing. Choose a home that meets your needs, with ownership rights confirmed for the buyer and the property.

sections.heading: Review the contract with the right documents
sections.body:
For each candidate, compare the sale agreement with the plan, specification and any written incentive. Ask what happens if the unit area or features differ from the agreement and how a dispute or defect is reported. Keep the original documents and any signed amendments together.

If a representative will sign, verify their authority and the registration department's requirements. Confirm which party will obtain clearance and submit the transfer or initial registration. Seek qualified advice if the contract contains a condition you cannot assess. A verbal assurance is not a substitute for the binding documents.

sections.heading: Ask for current options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Sharjah project collection](/projects?emirate=Sharjah) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, nationality and move date. Ask which ready or off-plan units are currently available and request their plans, terms and official documents.

Verify eligibility and all current charges before signing or paying.
